answers.d: when a bot follows links and downloads pages so a search engine can see them.
a query language for picking elements out of html or xml, the backbone of custom extraction in crawlers.
clickable references from one page to another, still the loudest signal of who vouches for whom.
a stored copy of a page or file, served again so nobody has to wait for the original.
south korea's biggest search engine, where google comes second.
the title tag, the line that usually becomes the blue link in search results.
a script attribute that downloads in parallel and runs only after the html is parsed.
the words someone types or says into a search box.
what tools call spammy backlinks, usually with more alarm than the links deserve.
the database of pages a search engine has stored and can return for a query.
a dns record that points one hostname at another, like www at the root domain.
a crawler; also the robots.txt file and meta robots tag that tell crawlers what to skip.
the moment pixels hit the screen, as in largest contentful paint, a core web vital.
search engine results pages, the thing every seo stares at all day.
a filter on a category page, like size or color, and a classic source of crawl waste.
a systematic check of a site for problems that cost traffic.
yahoo's old web crawler, named with a straight face.
the company name people search for; branded queries are the easiest clicks you'll ever get.
a passage of a page split out so an ai search system can retrieve and quote it on its own.
what happens when a searcher picks your result; ctr divides these by impressions.
a loading attribute value that tells the browser to fetch an image right away instead of lazily.
http over tls; the padlock, and a minor ranking signal since 2014.
the lookup that tells you who registered a domain and when it expires.
a picture on the page; alt text and file names help search engines understand it.
a slice of a search index stored on its own machine so lookups can run in parallel.
the small unit of text a language model reads and writes, roughly three quarters of a word.
showing search engines different content than users, a fast route to a manual action.
moving pictures; google shows them in their own carousels and key moments.
the cap on how many api calls or urls a tool lets you use per day.
a user agent string that identifies a browser or bot; also an ai that browses and acts for you.
index bloat: too many thin or duplicate urls indexed, diluting the pages that matter.
search with a place attached, where the map pack and business profile do the heavy lifting.
a script attribute that downloads in parallel and runs as soon as it arrives.
the trained system behind an ai answer; large language model is the full name.
dwell time: how long a searcher stays on a result before returning to the serp.
a single request for a url, by a browser or by a crawler.
a french search engine that sells itself on not tracking you.
regular expressions, the pattern language that makes search console filters actually useful.
the authorization protocol that lets a tool read your analytics without your password.
the t in e-e-a-t, which google calls the most important member of the family.
the august 2018 core update that hit health and finance sites hard.
a tiny tracking image or script that reports a visit or conversion back to a platform.
grouping related pages together in the site structure and internal links.
the subject a page covers; topical authority is covering one thoroughly enough to be trusted on it.
the 2009 google update that started favoring big brands for broad queries.
a javascript library for building interfaces; client-side rendering is where seo gets interesting.
the narrower page in a hub and spoke model, linking back to its pillar.
a narrow market or topic, the place most new sites have a fighting chance.
a country code top-level domain like .es or .de, a strong hint about target country.
a web framework that ships html first and javascript only where needed; it built this site.
content behind a form or login, which crawlers can't see.
the knowledge graph: google's database of entities and how they relate.
a web server and reverse proxy; its config is where many redirects live.
still the main channel for link outreach, and still mostly ignored.
compression that throws away some data for smaller files, like most jpeg and webp images.
a tracked interaction in ga4, from page views to purchases.
removing or consolidating weak pages so the rest of the site gets more attention.
a wordpress seo plugin, and for many people their first meta description box.
a schema.org type for step-by-step instructions, no longer shown as a rich result.
people who raised their hand; for b2b seo, the number the cfo actually asks about.
301 moved permanently, the status code that passes a page's signals to its new url.
the 2011 google update that went after thin and low-quality content.
how many clicks a page sits from the homepage; deeper pages get crawled less.
a guest post: an article written for another site, usually to earn a link.
a url parameter after the question mark, like ?utm_source or ?sort=price.
china's dominant search engine.
freshness: the preference for recent content on queries where recency matters.
the elements in a page's dom; too many slows rendering.
a redirect chain, where one url hops through several redirects before landing.
the outreach email asking a site to cover or link to you.
site reputation abuse: third-party content hosted to ride a strong site's rankings.
voice search: queries spoken to an assistant, usually longer and phrased as questions.
a list of numbers representing meaning, used to match passages to queries; short for embedding.
a number a tool assigns, like a lighthouse score; useful until it becomes the goal.
302 found, the status code for a temporary redirect.
page speed: how fast a page loads and becomes usable.
a q&a site that shows up in serps far more than anyone expected.
layout shift: content jumping as a page loads, measured as cumulative layout shift.
redirect loops: a url redirecting back to itself until the browser gives up.
first input delay, the old core web vital that inp replaced in 2024.
an overlay that covers content; intrusive ones on mobile can hurt rankings.
split testing: showing two versions of a page to see which performs better.
the original web portal, whose search results have been powered by bing since 2010.
the template that controls a cms site's design and often its markup.
the backend of a cms, where most seo fixes eventually get made.
finding out why something is broken; for seo, often why a page isn't indexed.
a 4xx or 5xx response; search console lists the ones crawlers hit.
a robots.txt directive that reopens a path inside a disallowed folder.
review stars in search results, powered by review schema.
a content brief: the instructions a writer gets before drafting.
search terms, the queries that actually triggered your page or ad.
seed keywords: the starting terms you expand into a full keyword list.
the shape of interest over time; google trends shows it for any query.
the knowledge panel, the info box google shows for an entity.
a discussion site; google started surfacing many more of them in 2023.
an html element for content tangential to the main content, like a sidebar.
an html attribute that labels elements for css and javascript.
css rules, inline or in a stylesheet, that control how a page looks.
an html element for tabular data, and a common source of featured snippets.
the units of page weight; fewer bytes, faster pages.
the list of urls a crawler has found but not yet fetched.
processing many urls or keywords at once instead of one by one.
exact match: a keyword or anchor that repeats the target term word for word.
broad match: a keyword setting that lets ads show for loosely related searches.
fuzzy matching: finding results that are close to the query despite typos.
a privacy browser with its own independent search index.
to read raw html or data and turn it into a structure a program can use.
compiling a site from source into the files that get deployed.
the path a url maps to in a web app, and the page it renders.
a server that sits between a client and the web, forwarding requests.
an iframe: a page embedded inside another page, usually credited to its own url.
images, video and audio; also the css media queries behind responsive layouts.
content or cached data that is out of date but still being served.
page views, the oldest metric in analytics.
a session: one person's stretch of activity on a site.
the people behind the sessions, as counted by analytics.
conversions in old universal analytics, now called key events in ga4.
the most generic type in schema.org, which every other type inherits from.
to teach a model on data; training data is where your content may end up.
digital pr: earning coverage and links from news sites.
share of voice: your slice of visibility across a set of keywords.
social cards: the preview image and text a link shows when shared.
a blogging cms; also ghost spam, fake referral traffic in old analytics.
functions that run at set points, like wordpress actions or react hooks.
the user action measured by interaction to next paint and first input delay.
blocking a path in robots.txt, which stops crawling but not always indexing.
rss or product feeds: structured lists of items for readers and shopping engines.
scaled content abuse: mass-producing pages mainly to rank, by hand or by ai.
an http method for partial updates, and the fix you ship after a bad deploy.
